at_rest.defends_against: a file-read-only primitive held by the non-root `git` account (a path traversal in the transport wrapper, say), for the two 0600 files. Also closes the /proc/<pid>/cmdline channel for both credentials: every POST passes its header via `curl -K -` on stdin, and both redactors read their sed script from a 0600 file rather than an -e operand, so no external process carries a secret in argv (cmdline is mode 444; environ is 400). ALSO, since #7772: CODE EXECUTION as a NON-ROOT account can no longer read user_data from the Hetzner metadata endpoint. A host-local nftables rule (write_files /usr/local/bin/git-data-nftables.sh + git-data-nftables.service, armed by a runcmd `systemctl enable --now`) drops 169.254.169.254 for `meta skuid != 0`. Measured on this host's image (Ubuntu 24.04 / nftables v1.0.9): root still reaches the endpoint, non-root is dropped, and an un-ruled control address still reaches. Root is exempt so cloud-init's own datasource is unaffected.
at_rest.does_not_defend: CODE EXECUTION AS ROOT, which reads user_data from the metadata endpoint exactly as before — the #7772 nftables drop is scoped to non-root UIDs by design (ADR-198's own wording), so it narrows this from 'any account' to 'root only'.
